9b388378710a657f29be5ba7a72ebd74db982c68: A resort on a human scale, Samoëns prioritises quality of welcome and closeness rather than impressive figures. Its 40 km of pistes are ideal for a 3–4 day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Samoëns's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for learning to ski with children. Samoëns's altitude (720 m at the base, 2480 m at the top) allows decent snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The budget for a stay in Samoëns is clearly high: 59€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It's the price of excellence — but be aware of it before you go. In short: Samoëns is one of those rare resorts that combines a real village, a sincere family atmosphere and pistes suited to everyone. It's hard to get your stay wrong here.

9bf57d5f68980cdf5a2e9b13b7f65f10afa57dd2: Werfenweng is a low-key resort on a modest scale: 29 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Werfenweng's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for getting children started on skiing. Werfenweng's moderate altitude (902 m at the base, 1834 m at the summit) makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the surest months for optimal snow cover. Outside that window, checking snow bulletins before you leave is strongly advised. A stay in Werfenweng is clearly expensive: 58€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Werfenweng doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
